headline: AI rebound and French riots nudge the dollar up; loonie leads on BoC hike bets, yen lags
summary: The dollar index rose about 0.15% to near 102.0 as a rebound in AI stocks pushed the US 10-year yield back to about 5.14% and violent protests in France knocked the euro to about 1.1215. The Canadian dollar, Aussie and won led on a hawkish Bank of Canada, China's GDP beat and exporter selling; the yen, rupiah, Taiwan dollar and peso lagged.
drivers: Weekend riots pushed the OAT–Bund spread to around 140–147bp, crisis-era levels, and the euro fell about 0.2% to near 1.1215 after a dip to 1.1181. Sterling hit a 17-month high against it near 83.95 pence.
AI rebound lifts yields and the dollar

Chip stocks ended a nine-day slide and the Nasdaq gained about 1.1%, so Treasuries sold off: the 10-year rose about 4bp to 5.14%. That widened rate gaps and made the yen the weakest major, with USD/JPY up about 0.3% to 158.5.
Hawks in Ottawa, outflows in Asia

Macklem's warning on energy inflation lifted Oct 28 BoC hike odds to about 80% from 30%, taking the loonie to a four-week high near 1.407. In Asia, MSCI's Indonesia threat, foreign selling of Taiwan shares and oil kept the rupiah, Taiwan dollar and peso under pressure.
view: Still mildly weaker into the Fed (Oct 28) and BoJ (Oct 30), but Monday showed where the floor is: a 10-year yield above 5.1% and a December Fed hike still largely priced keep dips shallow, so I expect the index to range between about 101 and 102.5 rather than break down. Fade the dollar against the yen and the Canadian dollar, where central banks are turning hawkish; stay long it against the Aussie and the rupiah. A Fed hold on Oct 28 that clearly endorses a December hike would make me neutral.
ideas: Best risk/reward: the upside is capped by Tokyo's 159–160 intervention zone while Ueda is prepping a hike; sell 158.50–159.00 for 156.80, about 2:1.
BoC hike odds jumped to about 80% for Oct 28 while the Fed is expected to hold; sell bounces into 1.4150–1.4180 for 1.3950.
MSCI's standalone threat means forced index selling and the 10-year yield hit 7.4%; buy dips toward 17,950 for a test of the 18,190 record.
review: Quiet session, no targets or stops hit: USD/JPY and USD/TWD shorts filled (TWD at its 32.57 high, now about 0.1 in favour), USD/IDR long is about 0.2% in favour, the EUR/USD long tested its 1.1180 entry and sits flat, ranges held; USD/CAD reset lower on the BoC, CNH and SGD levels adjusted for risk/reward.

eurusd.note: Fell about 0.2% to near 1.1215 on French riots, after a 1.1181 low in thin early Asian trade.

view.call: Buy dips toward 1.1180; a priced December ECB hike gives support.

eurusd.why: This was a euro move, not a dollar move. Weekend riots in France pushed the OAT–Bund spread to around 140–147bp, levels last seen in the 2011–12 debt crisis, and the CAC 40 fell more than 1%. The dollar added a little help as an AI-stock rebound lifted the 10-year Treasury yield to about 5.14%, leaving the euro near 1.1215 and well under the 1.1270 area that has capped it four times.
eurusd.outlook: I keep buying dips toward 1.1180: the dollar's rate support has stopped growing and a December ECB hike is priced. But France caps rallies near 1.1270 until spreads narrow, and a close under 1.114 would mean the French discount is winning.
eurusd.watch: French bond spreads and budget talks, then the Fed on Oct 28 and the ECB on Oct 29.

gbpusd.note: Steady near 1.3305; sterling hit a 17-month high against the euro on French turmoil.

view.call: 1.3200–1.3400; fade the top unless it closes above 1.3400.

gbpusd.why: Sterling is absorbing euro selling rather than outperforming the dollar. Money leaving the euro over France lifted the pound to a 17-month high near 83.95 pence per euro, while against a firmer dollar it slipped about 0.05% to near 1.3305. Recent upside surprises in UK data and fewer worries about UK public finances are keeping it supported.
gbpusd.outlook: A range trade against the dollar: HSBC and others see a hawkish Fed weighing on it, while the euro cross does the heavy lifting. Only a daily close above 1.3400 would change that.
gbpusd.watch: UK CPI on Oct 21 and Bank of England speakers, then the Fed on Oct 28.

audusd.note: Rose about 0.5% to near 0.698 on China's 4.5% GDP beat and the rebound in stocks.

view.call: Sell 0.6990–0.7020; a bounce, not a turn.

audusd.why: The Aussie led on risk appetite and China. Third-quarter Chinese growth came in at 4.5% against a 4.4% forecast, chip stocks bounced and the yuan's offshore rate hit its strongest since mid-2022, so investors bought growth-linked currencies. It rose about 0.5% to near 0.698, its second straight gain from last week's three-month low of 0.6894.
audusd.outlook: I still see this as a bounce to sell. Last week's jobs shock (unemployment 4.7%) took RBA hikes off the table while the Fed keeps hike risk, so I'd sell into 0.6990–0.7020; a close above 0.7070 would end the call.
audusd.watch: RBA minutes and speakers, China data, and the RBA decision on Nov 3.

usdjpy.note: Up about 0.3% to near 158.5 as Treasury yields rose; still inside last week's 157.55–158.94 range.
usdjpy.why: The dollar did the moving. A rebound in AI stocks sent the 10-year Treasury yield up about 4bp to 5.14%, widening the US–Japan rate gap and making the yen the weakest major on the day. That outweighed Governor Ueda's comments that underlying inflation is close to 2% and that hiking too slowly risks higher bond yields, and PM Takaichi's insistence she is not driving the weak yen.
usdjpy.outlook: Asymmetric: the upside is capped by the 159–160 zone where Tokyo has threatened action and joined the US in intervening in July, while swaps price about an 80% chance of a December BoJ hike. Selling 158.50–159.00 stays my best risk/reward; a close above 159.60 would say Tokyo is tolerating more weakness.
usdjpy.watch: Japan's September CPI on Oct 23, the Fed on Oct 28, the BoJ on Oct 30, and any rate checks near 159.

usdchf.note: Bounced about 0.35% to near 0.827 as the dollar firmed and haven demand eased with stocks.

view.call: Sell bounces toward 0.8300; the franc trend is intact.

usdchf.why: USD/CHF bounced to about 0.827 because the rebound in stocks reduced haven demand while higher Treasury yields helped the dollar. The franc still gained against the euro, which fell to a three-month low against it on France's unrest, so this was dollar strength rather than franc weakness. Markets continue to judge the SNB will hold at zero rather than go negative.
usdchf.outlook: The franc's trend remains firm, so I keep selling bounces toward 0.8300 rather than chasing; a close above 0.8360 would end the call.
usdchf.watch: European bond spreads, SNB comments on the franc, and the Fed on Oct 28.

usdcad.note: Loonie hit a four-week high near 1.4071 as BoC hike odds jumped to about 80%; closed near 1.411.

view.call: Sell bounces into 1.4150–1.4180; BoC hike risk.

usdcad.why: The loonie was driven by the Bank of Canada. Governor Macklem said on Saturday the bank will raise its inflation forecast significantly because of high oil and fuel prices, and swaps moved to about an 80% chance of an Oct 28 hike from 30% on Friday. That lifted the Canadian dollar to its strongest since Sept 23 near 1.4071, even as oil eased on US waivers for Russian fuel exports.
usdcad.outlook: I lower the call: with a BoC hike now likely and the Fed expected to hold, I'd sell bounces into 1.4150–1.4180 for 1.3950. The risks are Alberta's referendum and a sharp oil drop; a close above 1.4250 would end it.
usdcad.watch: Alberta's referendum result, Canada data, oil, and the BoC and Fed decisions on Oct 28.

usdcnh.note: Yuan near 6.682 offshore, strongest since mid-2022, after a GDP beat; the 6.7208 fix was the strongest since Feb 2023.

view.call: Slow grind lower at the PBOC's pace.

usdcnh.why: The yuan firmed slightly to about 6.682 after China's third-quarter GDP beat at 4.5%, driven by exports. The PBOC set its fixing at 6.7208, the strongest since February 2023, but still about 300 pips weaker than the 6.6897 Reuters estimate, so it keeps letting the yuan rise slowly while braking the pace. Governor Pan also flagged a shift to an overnight policy rate.
usdcnh.outlook: A slow grind lower in USD/CNH at Beijing's pace. I'm moving the target to 6.64 and the stop to 6.71, above last week's highs, for a better balance; a fix close to estimates would mean faster gains.
usdcnh.watch: Daily PBOC fixings versus estimates, the loan prime rate, and US–China trade headlines.

usdhkd.note: Pinned near 7.848, just shy of the 7.85 weak-side limit.

view.call: 7.84–7.85, no trade; an HKMA defence would lift HIBOR fast.

usdhkd.why: USD/HKD stayed near 7.848, close to the 7.85 weak edge of the peg. Low Hong Kong interest rates relative to the US make it cheap to borrow HKD and buy USD, and Monday's rise in Treasury yields only widened that gap.
usdhkd.outlook: No trade. A touch of 7.85 would force the HKMA to buy HKD, draining cash and pushing HIBOR up fast; that is the only catalyst that moves it.
usdhkd.watch: HKMA intervention at 7.85, the aggregate balance and one-month HIBOR.

usdsgd.note: Flat near 1.280, tracking the broad dollar; the S$NEER sits near the strong side of its band.

view.call: Mildly lower with the dollar; SGD is low-beta.

usdsgd.why: USD/SGD held near 1.280 as a firmer dollar against the euro and yen was offset by firmer Asian growth currencies after China's GDP beat. On Oct 14 the MAS surprised by holding its policy band, and the S$NEER sits about 1.6–1.7% above its midpoint, close to the strong edge, which limits further basket gains.
usdsgd.outlook: Mildly lower if the dollar eases into the Fed. I'm moving the target to 1.272 and the stop to 1.285 for a better reward-to-risk; SGD will lag other Asian currencies on any rally.
usdsgd.watch: Singapore CPI and trade data, and the broad dollar into the Fed on Oct 28.

usdkrw.note: Won firmed 1.1 to 1,330.3 at the Seoul close, after touching 1,327.6, its strongest since Oct 2024.

view.call: Sell rallies toward 1,345; needs chips to hold up.

usdkrw.why: The won rose to a two-year high intraday as exporters sold dollars and the Kospi reversed a 3% opening drop to close up 1.76% on institutional buying. Foreign investors were only small net sellers of about 37.8 billion won, a big change from last week's heavy selling, and the finance minister said the rate is now in line with fundamentals.
usdkrw.outlook: I keep selling USD/KRW rallies toward 1,345. The won tracks chip stocks and foreign flows, so this week's AI earnings matter; another big foreign selling day would push it back toward 1,360.
usdkrw.watch: Foreign flows in Seoul, Samsung and SK hynix, AI earnings this week, and Korea's Q3 GDP.

usdtwd.note: Taiwan dollar fell 0.107 to 32.445, after hitting 32.57, its weakest since April 2025.

view.call: Fade 32.50–32.60; the central bank has flagged action.

usdtwd.why: The Taiwan dollar extended last week's slide as foreign investors sold another NT$76.7 billion (about US$2.4 billion) of Taiwan shares and the Taiex slipped 0.6%. It touched 32.57 before the central bank said it may intervene to keep the currency stable, blaming last week's US$19.4 billion of foreign share sales and US$18 billion of outflows on the global chip sell-off.
usdtwd.outlook: The 32.50 area is the weak end of the range the central bank has defended this year, and it has now said so publicly; fading 32.50–32.60 offers the better risk/reward, provided chip stocks stop falling. A close above 32.80 would mean outflows are winning.
usdtwd.watch: Foreign flows on the Taiex, TSMC and AI earnings this week, and central bank action near 32.50.

usdmyr.note: Ringgit eased slightly to about 4.0825 at the 6pm close but gained on the euro, yen and ASEAN peers.
usdmyr.why: The ringgit barely moved against the dollar but rose against most others on strong Malaysian data: third-quarter growth beat forecasts at 5.3%, September inflation eased to 1.8%, and total trade jumped 53.7% from a year earlier. It also gained against the rupiah as Indonesia's MSCI scare pushed money out of Jakarta.
usdmyr.outlook: Range-bound around 4.07–4.10. Strong trade and low inflation support it, but it rarely moves far without the broad dollar.
usdmyr.watch: The Fed on Oct 28, oil prices, and Bank Negara's Nov 5 meeting.

usdphp.note: Peso closed at a record low of 63.09, down 10.5 centavos; it traded 62.98–63.17.

view.call: 62.80–63.40 into Thursday's BSP; a skip would break 63.40.

usdphp.why: The peso set its third record-low close this month even though oil eased. Brent near $108 keeps the Philippines' import bill high, the dollar firmed on higher Treasury yields, and the BSP is in its quiet period before Thursday's meeting. It is down about 6.8% this year.
usdphp.outlook: A 62.80–63.40 range into Thursday. Twenty of 22 economists expect a 25bp hike to 5.25%, and BPI sees a 50bp move if the peso nears 64; a hike should steady it, while a skip would likely break 63.40.
usdphp.watch: The BSP decision on Oct 22, oil prices, and BSP dollar sales near 63.20.

usdidr.note: Rupiah weakened to about 18,040 as Jakarta stocks fell another 3.6% on MSCI's expulsion threat.

view.call: Stay long dollar; buy dips toward 17,950.

usdidr.why: The rupiah was Asia's worst performer because of domestic flows, not the dollar. MSCI said on Friday it may move Indonesia to standalone status, forcing index funds out; Jakarta stocks fell to a six-year low after an 11.6% drop on Friday, and the 10-year bond yield jumped to about 7.4% from 7.17%. Bank Indonesia said it is intervening in spot, DNDF and offshore NDF markets.
usdidr.outlook: I stay long the dollar. Intervention, and possibly a hike on Wednesday that 14 of 29 economists expect or Citi's 50bp call, can slow the slide but probably not stop a test of the 18,190 record while the MSCI threat stands. Credible government steps to answer MSCI would end the call.
usdidr.watch: Bank Indonesia's decision on Oct 21, the government's response to MSCI, and bond auctions.

usdinr.note: Rupee closed about 94.92, little changed, after RBI dollar sales lifted it at the open.

view.call: 94.50–95.80; the RBI wants order, not a rally.

usdinr.why: The rupee opened firmer at about 94.86 on RBI dollar sales, extending last week's best run since March, but gave the gains back as Brent near $108 and foreign equity outflows lifted dollar demand from importers. Traders see 95 as the RBI's soft defence line.
usdinr.outlook: A managed range of 94.50–95.80. The RBI is aiming for stability rather than a rally, and oil is the main risk; I wouldn't chase it either way.
usdinr.watch: Oil prices, RBI intervention near 95, and foreign portfolio flows.

eurjpy.note: Little changed near 177.8 as euro weakness on France offset the yen's slide.

view.call: 176–179; the BoJ on Oct 30 is the event risk.

eurjpy.why: Both sides fell together: the euro on French unrest and wider bond spreads, the yen on higher US yields. With EUR/USD down about 0.2% and USD/JPY up about 0.3%, the cross ended near 177.8, barely changed.
eurjpy.outlook: Range 176–179. The ECB (Oct 29) and BoJ (Oct 30) meet back to back; a hawkish BoJ would break it lower, while a French budget deal would lift it.
eurjpy.watch: French bond spreads, Japan CPI on Oct 23, and the ECB and BoJ meetings.

cnhjpy.note: Firmed to about 23.72 as the yuan held its gains and the yen weakened.
cnhjpy.why: The yuan held near its strongest since mid-2022 after China's GDP beat, while the yen slipped on higher US yields, nudging CNH/JPY up to about 23.72, near the top of its recent range.
cnhjpy.outlook: No edge in a 23.3–23.8 range: the PBOC slows yuan gains while Tokyo guards the yen's weak side. A break above 23.8 would need the yen to weaken through 159.
cnhjpy.watch: PBOC fixings and Japanese intervention signals.

watch: Next: UK CPI and Bank Indonesia (Oct 21), the BSP (Oct 22), Japan CPI (Oct 23), the Fed and BoC (Oct 28), the ECB and BoJ (Oct 29–30), AI earnings this week, MSCI follow-up on Indonesia, and Tokyo's 159–160 line.
